ms.promise:
A new crate within the pallas-extras workspace providing composable, asynchronous building blocks for interacting with Cardano’s node-to-node networking layer. The peer manager will:
・Maintain the Handshake, Peer Sharing, and optionally Keep-Alive mini-protocols.
・Maintain a dynamic list of active and available peers.
・Provide APIs to manage connections and peer discovery.

The chain syncrhonizer will:
・Maintain the Chain Sync mini-protocol, keeping a valid state of the current blockchain block headers in memory.
・Allow syncing of block headers from upstream peers.
・Emit a stream of new tip updates or rollbacks.

The block fetcher will:
・Fetch blocks from upstream peers using the Block Fetch mini protocol.
・Request full blocks based on chain state.
・Send blocks to downstream peers on request.

As for both previous milestones, proper documentation will be enforced along with high test coverage.
Each component will be implemented as an independent asynchronous actor, composable with other components. CI with automated testing, formatting, and linting will also be implemented.
ms.criteria:
Correctness & Robustness of all 3 components:
Peer manager: From a clean start with a list of bootstrap peers provided, the peer manager is able to maintain connections with a configurable amount of peers. This will be ensured by conducting prolonged tests on preview and preprod testnets, and providing logs collected during the experimentation. A locally reproducible simulation will also be made available. This simulation will support dropping arbitrary messages, and will also simulate the loss of peer connections. The simulation report along with peer-manager logs will also be generable.
Chai
ms.report:
Another milestone completed!
As explained in the reviewer documentation, the repository contains reproducible instructions for assessing every implementation output. The following summarizes that documentation.
A. Output: Composable asynchronous Cardano network components.
Acceptance criteria: The new `network-components` crate provides independent actors for peer management, chain synchronization, and block fetching. The actors compose through transport traits, and run against both a deterministic simulator and the real Cardano node-to-node transport.
Evidence: The `network-components` library - https://github.com/carloskiki/pallas-extras/tree/M3/network-components
B. Output: Peer-management and fault-tolerant chain synchronization.
Acceptance criteria: The peer manager maintains configurable active and available peer sets, performs handshakes, and replaces failed connections. Chain Sync starts at a supplied intersection, validates linked headers, emits roll-forward and rollback events, and recovers from arbitrary retained rollbacks. Deterministic tests inject exact message drops, periodic drops, and forced connection loss.
Evidence: The deterministic 30,000-header run maintained four peers despite 204 dropped messages and 64 disconnected sessions, then recovered from a 10,000-header rollback with zero validation failures. The report and reproduction command are in https://github.com/carloskiki/pallas-extras/blob/M3/reviewing/M3.md#deterministic-acceptance-report
C. Output: Selected-range block fetching and an integrated partial node.
Acceptance criteria: The block-fetch actor requests ranges selected by synchronized chain state, validates the blocks, and exceeds the required 20,000 blocks/minute in the deterministic benchmark. The integrated example runs all three actors, writes length-prefixed blocks, shuts down, rereads the file, and verifies every framing boundary, byte sequence, and block/header association.
